label: is-fix-22-26
topic: Fix open issues #22 to #26 of fractastical/delphi
summary: None of the five issues is fully resolved: three are partly done, one has a moved target and one needs a decision from Amit. No Lean was run in this pass, so every statement about Lean files comes from reading text, not from the kernel. All five issues were open with no comments when read. I wrote two files under D:/Users/ashenoy00000/delphi-work/agents4/is-fix-22-26/: certificate-coverage.py (new script, run once) and RESOLUTION-22-26.md (per-issue notes and apply steps). Main facts: track 1 has no elimination certificate; the ThompsonLaws folder now lives in the public leanbio repo, not the application repo; leanbio's law sets stop at 1.6.0.

findings.claim: #22 Track 6 (flying fish): bring the evaluation framework up to law set 1.8.1 and reuse it: PARTLY - wrote and ran a coverage script that lists the elimination certificates per track and exits 1 if a track has none. Today t2, t3, t4, t5 and t6 each have at least one; t1 (reporter / Hill separability) has none, so the first checkbox is one theorem short. The script reads the newest law set file (1.8.1), which with lawset-diff.py covers the second checkbox once it is added to the track build. The t1 certificate was not written, and the existing ones were not re-run through check.sh.

findings.confidence: high for the counts (script output); the mapping of the hygromorph files to t5 is my assumption from the file name

lay_summary: The project writes rules of biology in a language a computer can check, and keeps a to-do list of open problems.
I looked at five of those problems and wrote a small program that counts, for each research track, how many 'this design is impossible' proofs exist.
Five tracks have one, but track 1 has none, so that job is not finished.
I also found that some proof files moved to a second public library, and that library is two versions behind on its list of rules.
One question only the project lead can answer: which of the two libraries is the master copy.

glossary.Lean: A computer language for writing maths proofs that a program checks line by line.
glossary.kernel: The small trusted core of Lean that decides whether a proof is really correct.
glossary.theorem: A statement that has been proved.
glossary.elimination certificate (rules_out theor: A proof that a particular design cannot work because it would break a known law.
glossary.law set: A numbered, frozen list of the laws the project currently relies on (for example 1.8.1).
glossary.pinned law: A law that is included in a given law set.
glossary.registry: The folder of records describing each law and where its proof lives.
glossary.axiom audit: A check of which basic assumptions a proof depends on; it exposes unfinished proofs.
glossary.sorryAx: Lean's marker for a proof with a hole in it.
glossary.Timoshenko ceiling: The upper limit on how much a two-layer strip can curl when one layer swells more than the other.
glossary.hygromorph: A material that changes shape when it gets damp or dry.
glossary.induced drag: The air resistance a wing pays for making lift.
glossary.aspect ratio: How long and narrow a wing or fin is.
glossary.elastic similarity: A rule for how the thickness of supports should grow with length so they bend the same amount.
glossary.enhancer: A stretch of DNA that turns a gene's activity up.
glossary.promoter: The stretch of DNA where reading of a gene starts.
glossary.rank reversal: Two things swapping places in an ordered list when conditions change.
glossary.monotone: Always going the same direction: more input never gives less output.
glossary.MPRA / STARR-seq: Lab methods that measure the strength of thousands of DNA switches at once.
glossary.null rate: How often something appears by chance alone, with no real effect.
glossary.source of truth: The one copy that everyone else is meant to follow.
glossary.Mathlib: The large shared library of maths already proved in Lean.
